script.hook: A friend says they cannot come to your party. What do you say back? Here is the word, and why it works.
points: First, say ざんねんです. It means, that is too bad. Now break it open. The first kanji means remain. The second kanji means thought. So it is a thought that stays with you.
Second, look at the first kanji alone. It reads, のこる. It means, to remain. Like, one cake remains on the table. One piece is left behind, just like that thought.
Third, the second kanji shows up again. Say, ねんのため. It means, just in case. Like, just in case, I will write it down. A small thought, to be safe.
script.takeaway: So remember this. Remain plus thought equals regret. One kanji pair, three useful phrases.
script.cta: Follow for one Japanese tip every day.

blocks.en: I cannot come to your party.

blocks.en: Just in case, I will write it down.

social.caption:
A friend cannot come to your party. Here is the word to say back, and why it works.

残念です (ざんねんです) = that is too bad.
残 (のこる) = remain
念 = thought
A thought that stays with you.

残る (のこる) = to remain: ケーキが一つ残っています。One cake remains.
念のため (ねんのため) = just in case: 念のため、メモします。Just in case, I will write it down.

Follow for one Japanese tip every day.
